name: Teneligliptin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Teneligliptin is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor cleared by both liver (CYP3A4, flavin monooxygenases) and kidney (15% to 22% unchanged in urine). Kidney impairment raises exposure only modestly (at most about 1.7-fold), and the Thai label, based on the Japanese originator, sets no kidney dose adjustment; hemodialysis removes about 16% of a dose. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The label reports kidney pharmacokinetics by severity without numeric thresholds or dose changes; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 20 mg once daily; may increase to 40 mg once daily with close monitoring (Thai SmPC).

The label gives no kidney dose adjustment; exposure (AUC) was about 1.25-, 1.68- and 1.49-fold higher in mild, moderate and severe impairment (Thai SmPC). Use the usual 20 mg dose; increase to 40 mg only with close monitoring.

hd: No dose change in the label; end-stage kidney failure AUC about 1.16-fold; hemodialysis removed 15.6% of the dose (Thai SmPC). Dialysis timing not critical.
pd: No PD data; no change expected from end-stage kidney failure data (AUC about 1.16-fold).
crrt: No data. Insulin is usual in critical illness.
dialyzable: Partly: hemodialysis removed 15.6% of the dose (Thai SmPC).
monitoring: Hypoglycemia with a sulfonylurea or insulin (lower their dose). Avoid with QT prolongation or torsades history; caution with class IA or III antiarrhythmics. Persistent severe abdominal pain (pancreatitis), intestinal obstruction in those with prior abdominal surgery (Thai SmPC).
